subjects: System-names (rules for formation of a system-name)

conventions.positive-golden: tests/conformance/<edition>/<name>.cob + <name>.out; the directory selects --std. First line a comment `*> ISO §<clause> <rule> — <what is exercised>`. Unique PROGRAM-ID per program (a stale same-named assembly is served otherwise). Deterministic output only. Do NOT edit any manifest.json — return the entry; the director registers it.
conventions.negative-golden: tests/conformance/negative/<name>.cob + <name>.err (the expected diagnostic substring, e.g. COBOLNET1560). FIRST line of the .cob MUST be `*> reject-at: <year> [<year> ...]`. Do NOT edit the negative manifest — return the entry.
conventions.test-ref-forms: conformance:<edition>/<case> (positive, spec-derived) · conformance:negative/<case> · unit:<Class>.<Method> · conformance-test:<Class>.<Method>. nist:/characterization: and any *_MatchesLegacy method are NOT spec-derived and cannot close a row.
conventions.compiler: src/Cobol.Net.Cli/bin/Debug/net10.0/cobol.exe <file.cob> --std <85|2002|2014|2023> --run  (run in a scratch dir; never dotnet build/test — the tree is shared and a guard refuses builds while a fleet is live).
conventions.citation-check: python scripts/spec/cite.py --check <clause> "<quoted text>"  — every § you cite, no exceptions.

rows.subject: Simple relation conditions
rows.adjudicator-notes: Item 2 'Two operands of class alphabetic' with §8.8.4.2.1 'A class alphabetic operand shall be treated as though it were an operand of class alphanumeric' (cite.py OK). ForComparison routes alphabetic to the alphanumeric arm (§8.8.4.2.7). Measured: PIC A(3) 'ABC' < 'ABD' TRUE; = PIC X(5) 'ABC' TRUE (space extension). No spec-derived test isolating two alphabetic operands located. [editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (general-relation text carried unchanged into ISO/IEC 1989:2023; no Annex E entry — Annex E scopes only 2014->2023)]

rows.subject: Simple relation conditions
rows.adjudicator-notes: Item 3 'Two operands of class alphanumeric' + the group sentence ('an alphanumeric group item shall be treated as an elementary alphanumeric data item', cite.py OK). Measured: X(5) 'ABC' = 'ABC  ' TRUE, = SPACES FALSE; group G1 ('AB'+9(2) 12) = 'AB12' TRUE and > 'AB1' TRUE (space-extended); numeric-edited ZZ9 = ' 12' TRUE and '-1' > ' 1' TRUE (NOTE: numeric-edited compares alphanumerically). Collating-sequence detail belongs to §8.8.4.2.7's rows. Many goldens exercise it; none located whose header derives item 3 specifically, so test-ref left empty. [editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (general-relation text carried unchanged into ISO/IEC 1989:2023; no Annex E entry — Annex E scopes only 2014->2023)]

rows.subject: Simple relation conditions
rows.adjudicator-notes: Item 5 'Two operands of class national' -> §8.8.4.2.9. ForComparison returns National when either side is national. Measured: N(3) N"ABC" < N"ABD" TRUE; GROUP-USAGE NATIONAL group NG (N"AB") = N"AB  " TRUE and < N"AC" TRUE — the national-group-as-elementary sentence holds. National collating-sequence ordering is §8.8.4.2.9's rows. [editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (class national enters with ISO/IEC 1989:2002)]

rows.subject: Simple relation conditions
rows.adjudicator-notes: Item 7 'Two operands of different classes where each operand is from the set of classes alphanumeric, alphabetic, or national' -> §8.8.4.2.6 (alphanumeric converted to national). Measured: N(3) N"ABC" = X(5) 'ABC' TRUE, = A(3) 'ABC' TRUE; national group NG = X(2) 'AB' TRUE; alphabetic vs alphanumeric TRUE. PB649 (national figurative vs alphanumeric under a PCS) landed. [editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 for alphanumeric/alphabetic; the national member from 2002]
rows.rule-text: Two operands of different classes where each operand is from the set of classes alphanumeric, alphabetic, or national.

rows.subject: Simple relation conditions
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule (cite.py --check 8.8.4.2.13 "two index-names. The result is the same as if the corresponding occurrence numbers were compared" -> OK §8.8.4.2.13 1)). Code: an index-name operand binds to BoundComputedOperand(BoundIndexRef), whose value is the OCCURRENCE NUMBER, and the pair reaches RenderNumericRelational (§8.8.4.2.4 algebraic compare) — so two index-names compare by occurrence number irrespective of their tables' element sizes. Probe E:\Temp\claude\E--CobolSharp\a700c052-f9e4-4942-84ff-a13c7505d6ec\scratchpad\adj-d2\out\probe\srcp2\idx1.cob: I1 (table of X(4)) and I2 (table of X(8)) both SET TO 3 -> I1 = I2 TRUE (a displacement representation would say FALSE); I1 = J1 (same table) TRUE; after SET I2 TO 4: I1 < I2 TRUE, I2 > I1 TRUE; EVALUATE I1 WHEN I2 -> no match. No existing test pins two index-names of DIFFERENT element sizes (the case that distinguishes occurrence-number from displacement comparison) — test-needed. The 'only between' restriction of the clause stem is adjudicated on rows 2 and 3. [editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (index-names and their relation tests are in every edition)]
rows.rule-text: two index-names. The result is the same as if the corresponding occurrence numbers were compared.

rows.subject: Simple relation conditions
rows.adjudicator-notes: SR3 (cite.py OK). The only literal class outside the list is boolean: a boolean literal against a numeric item (`IF NI = B"1"`) and ALL boolean against alphanumeric (`IF X1 = ALL B"1"`) are refused COBOLNET0844; alphanumeric, hex, national, numeric literals and alphanumeric figuratives are accepted. A boolean literal against a boolean operand is a Format-2 relation, not Format 1. (Two-literal relations are GR-13's prose rule, not SR3.) No negative golden located isolating a boolean LITERAL in a general relation. [editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (boolean literals, the excluded class, exist from 2002)]
rows.rule-text: All literals shall be of class alphanumeric, national, or numeric.

rows.subject: Simple sign condition
rows.adjudicator-notes: Both printed formats reduce to `operand IS? NOT? (POSITIVE|NEGATIVE|ZERO)`: comparisonExpression alt 3 (written form) and partialComparison alt 2 (EVALUATE SR5 elided operand). The keyword is ZERO only; ZEROS/ZEROES are refused (PB510 landed, COBOLNET2418). IS is optional, NOT is optional, and one of the three keywords is required, which matches both diagrams. Probed with the pinned cobol.exe (probe dir out/probe/sign (p1b.cob, p2.cob, p3.cob, p4.cob)): Format 1 over a signed display item and over expressions (N + 1, N * 0, - N, N * -2 under --std 85), with IS NOT; Format 2 over bare FLOAT-BINARY-64/-32 names; EVALUATE FB WHEN NEGATIVE. All parse and bind. Which FORMAT an operand selects is SR1/SR2's partition and is adjudicated there (it diverges: see SR-8.8.4.7.3-2). test-ref left empty: conformance:2023/pb171_sign_condition_operands covers Format 1 only. conformance:2002/ca8_float_sign_format2 uses FLOAT-LONG, which is not a Format 2 operand at all (§3.166/§3.167), so no golden exercises Format 2 with a standard float usage. cite.py --check 8.8.4.7.3 SR1/SR2 OK. [editions as adjudicated: Format 1: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023. Format 2 (data-name-1 of a standard floating-point usage; the §3.166/§3.167 usages were introduced in 2014): 2014, 2023.]
rows.rule-text:
**Format 1 (expression)** 
 ╭ POSITIVE ╮ │ │ arithmetic-expression-1 IS [ NOT ] ┤ NEGATIVE ├ │ │ ╰ ZERO ╯
> **Figure notes (simple sign condition Format 1 (expression) syntax diagram).** `NOT`, `POSITIVE`, `NEGATIVE`, and `ZERO` are underlined in the printed standard (required words); `IS` is not underlined. No choice indicators appear in this figure. **Format 2 (standard-float)** 
 ╭ POSITIVE ╮ │ │ data-name-1 IS [NOT ] ┤ NEGATIVE ├ │ │ ╰ ZERO ╯
> **Figure notes (simple sign condition Format 2 (standard-float) syntax diagram).** `NOT`, `POSITIVE`, `NEGATIVE`, and `ZERO` are underlined in the printed standard (required words); `IS` is not underlined. No choice indicators appear in this figure.

rows.subject: Subscripts
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule (cite.py --check 8.4.2.3.3 'Qualified-data-name-1 and qualified-condition-name-1 are defined in 8.4.2.2, Qualification.' -> OK §8.4.2.3.3 1)): a definitional cross-reference - the subscripted reference's base is an ordinary §8.4.2.2 qualified name. Code: the dataReference carries OF/IN qualification before (and the grammar also after) the subscript group; ReferenceResolver resolves the base by the §8.4.2.2 FindItem over the written qualifiers, and qualified identifiers INSIDE a subscript (subscriptQualification) resolve the same way. Probe scratchpad/adj-d2/out/probe/subscripts/sr1a.cob (pinned cobol.exe, 2023): `MOVE "Z" TO E OF G2 (W OF G3)` / `MOVE "Q" TO E IN G1 (W IN G4)` over two same-named tables and two same-named subscripts -> `AAQBZB` (correct occurrence of the correct table each time); qualified condition-names `CB OF E OF G2 (1)` / `CB OF G2 (2)` evaluate correctly; the unqualified `E (1)` draws COBOLNET1639 (§8.4.2.2 uniqueness). No spec-derived test targets this row by name - CONFORMS-untested.
rows.rule-text: Qualified-data-name-1 and qualified-condition-name-1 are defined in 8.4.2.2, Qualification.

rows.subject: Subscripts
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule (cite.py --check 8.4.2.3.3 'ALL shall not be specified if qualified-condition-name-1 is specified.' -> OK §8.4.2.3.3 7)). No path admits ALL on a condition-name: the only two ALL-admitting contexts (§8.4.2.3.3 SR6) take a data item (intrinsic argument / SORT data-name-2), and everywhere else the ALL segment fails the subscript parse. Probes scratchpad/adj-d2/out/probe/subscripts/sr7a-d.cob over `05 E1 PIC 9 OCCURS 3. 88 C1 VALUE 1.`: `IF C1(ALL)`, `SET C1(ALL) TO TRUE`, `EVALUATE TRUE WHEN C1(ALL)` -> COBOLNET2363; `FUNCTION MAX(C1(ALL))` -> COBOLNET1639 (a condition-name identifies no data item); legal `IF C1(2)` / `IF C1 OF E1 (3)` run (sr7e). Every illegal spelling is refused at compile time; the COBOLNET2363 text names SR6 rather than SR7 (diagnostic wording only - SR6 independently forbids each of these). No test targets the condition-name spelling - CONFORMS-untested.
rows.rule-text: ALL shall not be specified if qualified-condition-name-1 is specified.

rows.subject: System-names (rules for formation of a system-name)
rows.adjudicator-notes: Optional item PROVIDED (one restriction), not 'not provided': §8.3.2.3.1 lets the implementor add restrictions to COBOL-word formation, and an all-digit system-name - a legal COBOL word, since §8.3.2.2's 'at least one basic letter' binds user-defined words only - is rejected (the lexer reads it as an integer literal). cite.py --check 8.3.2.3.1 'The implementor may define rules for the formation of a system-name that add restrictions to the rules for formation of a COBOL word' -> OK. Probes refute-probe/p198: sn3.cob OBJECT-COMPUTER. 12345. -> COBOL0001 unexpected '12345'; d1.cob OBJECT-COMPUTER. 1-2. -> OK (no letter needed); sn.cob 123ABC / MY_BOX-9-... -> OK at 2023; sn4.cob ABC- -> COBOL0001; sn5.cob 31/32 chars -> COBOLNET1567 limit 30 at 85, 31 at 2002/2014; sn2.cob 64 chars -> COBOLNET1567 limit 63 at 2023; dv.cob unknown device FOO-DEVICE -> COBOLNET2241. Owning note: kb/Work/PB1534, PB280.
rows.rule-text: System-names (rules for formation of a system-name). This item is optional. This item, if provided by the implementor, shall be documented in the implementor's user documentation. (8.3.2.3, System-names)
